pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Acute Intermittent Porphyria (AIP) THE SMOKING GUN: Urine oxidizing to a dark port-wine color upon light exposure, accompanied by severe abdominal pain without peritoneal signs, SIADH-induced hyponatremia, and acute motor-predominant polyneuropathy precipitated by caloric restriction. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: Acute Intermittent Porphyria is an autosomal dominant inborn error of heme biosynthesis caused by a deficiency of porphobilinogen deaminase (hydroxymethylbilane synthase). Severe fasting and metabolic stress induce hepatic ALAS1 (delta-aminolevulinic acid synthase 1), causing a massive accumulation of the upstream, neurotoxic heme precursors delta-aminolevulinic acid (ALA) and porphobilinogen (PBG). Elevated ALA leads to central, autonomic, and peripheral neurotoxicity, manifesting as autonomic instability (hypertension, tachycardia), neurovisceral abdominal pain, hypothalamic involvement with SIADH, and axonal motor neuropathy culminating in respiratory failure. Upon oxidation in air and light, PBG polymerizes into porphobilin, yielding the pathognomonic dark port-wine urine.
